editorial:
The Lone Ranger is Republic Pictures' 15-chapter serial, released February 12, 1938 and directed by William Witney and John English. Its chapters run from "Hi-Yo Silver" to "The Last of the Rangers". A creator might want it for its Western serial action and its place in the history of the character.

The rights question is the character, not just the film. Republic made the serial under a June 1937 contract with George W. Trendle. The copyright status of the underlying radio and character material was not checked, so it should be treated as a separate question from the film's own status. This dossier did not confirm the film's renewal status, so no layer is cleared. Check the 1965-1966 renewal records before reusing it, starting with the 1966 CCE volumes.
faq: Can I use clips from the 1938 serial?

Not yet. No renewal search was completed for the film, so its print status is unconfirmed. Search the CCE renewal volumes (1966 first) and the Copyright Office catalog first. The rights in the underlying Lone Ranger character material were not checked and may be separate.
Does the film's status clear the Lone Ranger character?

No. The serial was made under a June 1937 contract between Republic and George W. Trendle. The film's copyright status and the character's rights are separate questions, and the character side was not checked.
